- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for downward momentum.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 1.5x recent high or 20% below true peak.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion after a spike, model often fails to correct; apply 1–3% downward adjustment in subsequent periods.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values before applying sentiment-weighted adjustment.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of lagged sentiment to forecast adjustment (e.g., use sentiment from 3–5 days prior).
